summary: Tests only. One new RED file, apps/cli/src/runtime/outbound.publicationPrecondition.test.ts (4 tests), pins that `send` presupposes `relay publish`: an unpublished profile's send is refused LOCALLY, before any relay request is issued, so the recipient's single first-contact one-time prekey is never spent by a send the relay is certain to refuse; the error is a typed OutboundError named SENDER_NOT_PUBLISHED, ordered after the pre-existing CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED check; and the refused send leaves no claim id, no session and no outbox record behind. Every test asserts on the requests actually ISSUED, not only on the thrown error. test/e2e/publication-claimability.test.ts step 5 was not deleted but strengthened: the unpublished sender's attempt now happens BEFORE the bundle is consumed, and the real relay binary is the witness - `relay publish` must still report the recipient's bundle as claimable afterwards. Its original /PREKEY/ exhausted-prekey assertion is kept verbatim, moved behind a `relay publish` for that same sender. Ten fixture files that encoded a starting state which cannot succeed anyway were corrected by making the sending profile publish first; none was weakened, skipped, narrowed or deleted. Correctness of the corrections was established by a throwaway product probe (Profile.hasPublication + one guard in sendOwned) which took the whole apps/cli suite to 45 files / 253 tests / 0 failures; the probe was then fully reverted and both product files are byte-identical to baseline (outbound.ts 337031b1..., profile.ts 29c654f2...).

acceptance.criterion: New RED tests pin that a send from an unpublished profile refuses before issuing any claim, that no claim request reaches the relay, that the recipient's bundle stays claimable, and that the error is typed and actionable
acceptance.evidence: apps/cli/src/runtime/outbound.publicationPrecondition.test.ts, 4 tests, all RED on their own assertion: (1) 'a send that cannot be accepted must refuse before it issues any request, above all the claim: expected [ /v2/prekeys/claim, /v1/messages/send ] to deeply equal []'; (2) 'a refused send must not have claimed anything: expected 1 to be +0'; (3) 'a refused send must not commit an outbox envelope: expected [ cli:outbox:... ] to deeply equal []'; (4) 'expected UNAUTHORIZED_MAILBOX_ACCESS to be SENDER_NOT_PUBLISHED'.

acceptance.criterion: Assertions are on the requests actually issued, not only on the thrown error
acceptance.evidence: Tests 1 and 4 assert relay.paths() === [] and relay.claimsIssued() === 0; test 2 asserts exactly one claim in total and that it belongs to the sender that delivered; test 3 asserts the durable store carries no cli:claim:, cli:outbox: or session: key. Test 1 additionally asserts the relay fake's remaining available bundle is non-null.

acceptance.criterion: e2e step 5 re-stated as the stronger property rather than deleted
acceptance.evidence: publication-claimability.test.ts now runs carol's unpublished send at step 3, BEFORE anything has consumed bob's bundle, then asserts at step 4 that bob's `relay publish` still reports claimable === true with the identical bundleId - the real relay binary attesting that no claim reached it. The original assertions (not PROTOCOL_REJECTED, matches /PREKEY/) are kept verbatim as step 7, from a carol who has published. RED on the load-bearing assertion: 'an unpublished sender's refused send must leave the recipient's first-contact bundle intact: expected false to be true'.

acceptance.criterion: Blocked fixtures corrected minimally and without weakening
acceptance.evidence: 10 fixture files corrected. In every case the correction is either (a) the sending profile calling publish()/`relay publish` before it sends, or (b) adding a /v2/prekeys/publish route to a relay fake that previously threw on it. No assertion was removed or relaxed; two request-sequence assertions in outbound.test.ts were extended to include the new publish request, which pins strictly more than before. Measured: under the throwaway guard probe the full suite is 45 files / 253 tests / 0 failures.

FIXTURE. sha256 before: de0b4877d5af612bae352eba217250e1a646aa497933d2e11d5036d0218c7d98. after: 58d0dd98cdb94c8122eabdb7f204f3784bbf81be95d49d1fa6156d5c1f0c0921. Four tests now call publish() before sending. Not a weakening: their subjects are a SUCCESSFUL send, a trust decision on a CLAIMED bundle, an AMBIGUOUS deposit and an IDEMPOTENT replay - all of which require the send to reach the relay. The two request-sequence assertions were extended from [claim, send] to [publish, claim, send] and from [claim] to [publish, claim], which pins strictly more of the traffic than before; the claim and send bodies are now located by path rather than by index, so the same bodies are asserted.

Not a weakening: the fake still throws on every OTHER unexpected path, and this file's subject is T50 sender authentication - the envelope signature verifying against the profile's own PUBLISHED device record - so publishing first is the scenario, not a concession. All signature, binding-tamper and replay assertions are untouched.
